text:
Maria Pacheco: Heads up — ACME's renewal team just surfaced a contract ask: 99.95% E2E latency SLA for our hosted text-generation API + pinned model version. Renewal deadline in 3 weeks. Thoughts on prioritization?

Ajay Singh: yikes. Is this a hard requirement or negotiation leverage?

Maria Pacheco: Sales says they're firm unless we give a price concession. It's a top-10 logo and ~2x ARR if we keep them.

Sophia Lee: We need to break down what "E2E latency" means here. Is it 95th/99th token latency, or total request round-trip including network + app?

Dylan Ortiz: From infra side, guaranteeing 99.95% tail for hosted gen at scale is expensive. Could meet for dedicated pools or a dedicated SLA tier.

Ajay Singh: Suggest we run a quick RICE-ish triage to compare options (small calc in thread):
```
Reach: ACME (and comparable large renewals) = 1-2 deals/year
Impact: High (revenue retention) = 8
Confidence: 60% (we can build parts) = 6
Effort: 6 (infra + product + legal) => RICE ~ (1*8*6)/6 = 8
```
This is rough but shows high priority vs other mid-size roadmap items.

Sophia Lee: Also factor product risk — pinning model version adds maintenance/hotfix burden. We need rollout/rollback criteria in the contract.

Maria Pacheco: Good point. Sales asking for "pinned model + fallback to older model if issues". Ops worried about compatibility.

Dylan Ortiz: Operationally we can implement routing policies: pinned model on a dedicated pool, automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant in other regions. But that needs dedicated capacity + observability hooks. Estimate 3 sprint effort for a minimal safe path.

Sophia Lee: For prioritization, can we propose a middle-ground: SLA for a "dedicated tier" (higher price) + renewal clause for a temp commitment while we ship private options? That reduces org-wide SLA impact.

Ajay Singh: Agreed. Framing negotiable options: (A) Dedicated SLA (higher price, guaranteed pool), (B) Commercial SLA with exceptions for model-level regressions, (C) Temporary pilot SLA + roadmap milestone. We should score these against RICE and sequencing.

Maria Pacheco: Action items: 1) Product: write minimal acceptance criteria for dedicated SLA (SLO definitions, fallback policies, pinned model lifecycle). 2) Infra: quick feasibility + rough cost delta. 3) Sales: push for dedicated-tier pricing while we scope longer-term product changes.

Sophia Lee: I'll draft acceptance criteria. Minimal must-haves: clear metrics (p99 latency, error rate), allowed maintenance windows, model pin TTL, and automated rollback triggers.

Dylan Ortiz: I'll put together a cost/throughput sketch and a safe rollout plan (canary thresholds, cooldowns).

renewals-bot: Reminder: ACME renewal meeting scheduled 2/Mar 2026 16:00 PT.

Ajay Singh: One more thing — set launch criteria that link to regression tests & evals for pinned models. If a pinned model fails quality gates, contract should allow temporary switch to next approved variant.

Maria Pacheco: Agree. Let's aim to have a proposal for Sales by EOD Friday so they can negotiate terms. Quick sync tomorrow 10am?

Sophia Lee: 10am works for me.

Dylan Ortiz: 10am good. I'll bring cost numbers.

Ajay Singh: I'll help with the RICE comparison vs other roadmap bets.

Maria Pacheco: Thanks team — want this prioritized but not at the expense of the Q2 infra roadmap. We'll use the RICE + sequencing notes to justify scope tradeoffs to execs.

Sophia Lee: Keeping contract language tight will buy us runway. I'll include fallback/rollback wording in the draft.

Dylan Ortiz: Also recommend adding a monthly usage cap for the SLA pool to limit exposure during spikes.

Maria Pacheco: Good call. OK, talk tomorrow.
